categories.name: Spanners & Wrenches
categories.description: Combination, open-end, ring and slogging spanners, adjustable and pipe wrenches.
categories.how_to_choose: Match the spanner to the fastener size marked on the nut or bolt head. Use ring or combination spanners for high torque, open-end spanners where access is from the side, and slogging spanners only for striking. Chrome vanadium spanners with a chrome finish resist corrosion in humid coastal plants.
categories.care: Keep spanners clean and dry, never extend them with a pipe for extra leverage, and replace any spanner with a spread or cracked jaw.

categories.name: Pliers & Cutters
categories.description: Combination, long nose, side cutting, circlip, locking and water pump pliers, crimpers and strippers.
categories.how_to_choose: Choose combination pliers for general work, long nose for tight spaces, side cutters for flush cutting and circlip pliers for retaining rings. For electrical work, use pliers with proper insulated sleeves and never on live circuits unless they are VDE-rated.
categories.care: Oil the joint occasionally, do not use pliers as a hammer, and do not cut hardened wire with pliers not rated for it.

categories.name: Screwdrivers & Bits
categories.description: Screwdriver sets, precision drivers, bit sets and line testers.
categories.how_to_choose: Fit matters more than anything: the tip should fill the screw slot or recess completely. Phillips and Pozidriv are not interchangeable. Sets give the best coverage; single drivers replace your most-used sizes.
categories.care: Do not use screwdrivers as pry bars or chisels, and replace drivers with worn or rounded tips to avoid damaging screws.

categories.name: Sockets, Ratchets & Torque
categories.description: Socket sets in 1/4", 3/8" and 1/2" drive, ratchets and torque wrenches.
categories.how_to_choose: Pick the drive size by fastener size: 1/4" for small fasteners, 3/8" for general work, 1/2" for heavier bolts and 3/4" or 1" for trucks and machinery. Use six-point sockets for high torque and impact-rated sockets only with impact wrenches. Use a torque wrench wherever a tightening value is specified.
categories.care: Store torque wrenches at their lowest setting and have them calibrated periodically.

categories.name: Allen / Hex Keys
categories.description: L-keys, ball-point, folding and ring hex key sets.
categories.how_to_choose: Check whether your fasteners are metric or inch before buying. Ball-point keys allow angled entry; long-arm keys add reach and leverage.
categories.care: Use the correct size fully inserted to avoid rounding the socket head.

categories.name: Hammers & Striking
categories.description: Ball pein, claw, soft-face and rubber mallets.
categories.how_to_choose: Ball pein hammers suit metalwork, claw hammers suit nailing, and soft-face or rubber mallets protect finished surfaces. Choose weight by task: lighter for precision, heavier for driving.
categories.care: Check that the head is tight on the handle before use and replace damaged handles.

categories.name: Measuring & Levels
categories.description: Measuring tapes, spirit levels and chalk lines.
categories.how_to_choose: Short steel tapes suit shop-floor use, long tapes suit site layout. For levels, longer beams give more accurate readings over a distance; magnetic levels hold onto steel structures.
categories.care: Keep levels in their case and check accuracy by reversing the level on a flat surface.

categories.name: Knives, Saws & Snips
categories.description: Utility knives, blades, bolt cutters, aviation snips and hacksaw frames.
categories.how_to_choose: Snap-off knives suit packaging and light cutting, utility knives suit heavier materials, and snips or bolt cutters handle metal. Match bolt cutter length to the thickness of material to be cut.
categories.care: Always retract or cover blades after use and dispose of used blades safely.

categories.name: Tool Kits & Storage
categories.description: Ready tool kits, tool boxes, bags and trolleys.
categories.how_to_choose: Ready kits are the fastest way to equip a new technician. Cantilever boxes display everything at once, plastic boxes are light to carry, and roller cabinets suit a fixed workshop bay.
categories.care: Label drawers and use foam or trays so missing tools are noticed.

categories.name: Workshop & Lifting
categories.description: Clamps, bench vices, jacks, grease guns and hand trucks.
categories.how_to_choose: Choose jacks with capacity above the load you lift, and always use stands under raised loads. Pick hand truck capacity to suit your heaviest regular load.
categories.care: Never work under a load supported only by a jack.

categories.name: Pneumatic Components
categories.description: Solenoid valves, FRL units, cylinders, push-in fittings, PU tubing and couplers.
categories.how_to_choose: Size fittings and tubing to the port thread (1/8", 1/4", 3/8", 1/2") and tube OD (4 to 16 mm). For valves, choose 5/2 for double acting cylinders and 3/2 for single acting, and confirm the coil voltage. For cylinders, choose bore by force (force ≈ pressure × piston area) and stroke by travel.
categories.care: Install an FRL ahead of valves and cylinders; dry, clean air is the biggest factor in pneumatic component life.
faqs: Are Techno push-in fittings compatible with other brands of PU tube?
Yes. Push-in fittings are sized by tube outer diameter (4, 6, 8, 10, 12 mm and so on), so any good-quality PU or nylon tube of the same OD will fit.

categories.name: Air Tools
categories.description: Air impact wrenches, die grinders, angle grinders, spray guns and blow guns.
categories.how_to_choose: Check the tool's air consumption (SCFM) against your compressor output and use a hose of adequate size. Choose impact wrench drive and torque by the largest fastener you handle.
categories.care: Oil air tools daily (unless lubricated by an FRL), drain the compressor tank, and wear eye and hearing protection.
faqs: What compressor do I need for an air impact wrench?
Most 1/2" impact wrenches need about 4 to 8 SCFM at 6.3 bar. Check the tool's rating and allow extra capacity if several tools run at once.

categories.name: Brass Fittings
categories.description: Brass hose nipples, elbows, tees, unions, PU connectors and valves.
categories.how_to_choose: Identify thread size and gender (male/female) on both components. Hose nipples are sized by thread × hose bore. Use PTFE tape or thread sealant on tapered threads.
categories.care: Do not over-tighten brass fittings; brass is softer than steel and threads can strip.
faqs: Yes, the fittings are made with BSP threads in inch sizes. Confirm parallel (BSPP) or tapered (BSPT) with our team for critical applications.

categories.name: Taps & Drills
categories.description: HSS hand taps, TiN-coated taps, pipe taps and HSS jobber drills.
categories.how_to_choose: Match the tap to the thread standard (metric coarse, BSW, BSP, NPT) and drill the correct tap drill size first. Use hand taps in sequence for blind holes and spiral point taps for through holes on machines. TiN-coated taps last longer on steel.
categories.care: Always use cutting oil and back the tap off regularly to break chips when hand tapping.
faqs: What is the tap drill size for M8 × 1.25?
6.8 mm. As a rule for metric coarse threads, tap drill ≈ nominal diameter minus pitch.
